FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A43
An eight-sided traffic sign has the meaning STOP. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A43
A triangular traffic sign has the meaning YIELD. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A43
A diamond-shaped warning identifies a special condition or hazard ahead and calls for slower, cautious travel. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A43
Vertical rectangular signs generally give legal instructions or regulatory information. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A43
Horizontal rectangular signs provide directions or other information. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A43
A five-sided school sign marks a school zone or warns about a schoolchildren's crossing. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A43
A pennant-shaped sign identifies a no-passing zone. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A43
Crossbuck and circular railroad warnings call for looking both ways, listening and yielding to trains, with readiness to stop for an approaching train. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A43
A number displayed below a crossbuck indicates that the crossing has multiple tracks. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A43
Stop at flashing railroad lights and do not cross until the crossing is safe. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A43
At a multiple-track crossing, watch for another train moving in either direction. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A43
At a gated crossing, stop when the warning lights begin flashing rather than waiting for the gate to lower. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A43
Remain stopped until the railroad gates have risen and the warning lights have stopped flashing. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A43
Driving around a lowered railroad gate is dangerous and unlawful. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A44
Regulatory signs state traffic-law requirements that drivers are expected to obey. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A44
A red circle crossed by a slash prohibits the activity represented by its symbol. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A44
A stop sign requires a full stop before entering the intersection. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A44
Where a stop line is painted, stop at that line. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A44
Stop before a crosswalk, whether or not the crossing is painted. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A44
With no crosswalk, stop at the nearest safe point before the intersecting road where approaching traffic can be seen clearly. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A44
At a yield sign, slow down and stop if needed to give crossing or merging traffic the right of way. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A44
A speed-limit sign gives the maximum lawful roadway speed. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A44
A No Left Turn sign prohibits a left turn. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A44
A No Right Turn sign prohibits a right turn. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A44
A No U-Turn sign prohibits a reversal by U-turn. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A45
Do not drive beyond a Wrong Way or Do Not Enter sign; these often mark a one-way road or expressway ramp. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A45
A One Way sign permits traffic only along the arrow's direction. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A45
A No Parking sign prohibits parking at the signed location. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A45
A center lane marked Left Turn Only may be used only for making a left turn. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A45
A Keep Right sign directs traffic to the right of the island, median or obstruction ahead. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A45
Slower Traffic Keep Right signs help limit weaving and discourage below-normal-speed travel in the left lanes of multilane roads. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A46
A Signal Ahead warning calls for readiness to stop at an approaching traffic signal. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A46
A Reduce Speed Ahead sign warns that a lower-speed zone is approaching. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A46
Stop Ahead warns that a stop sign is approaching. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A46
Yield Ahead warns that a yield sign is approaching. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A46
Divided Highway Begins warns of a median or divider separating one-way traffic lanes and directs drivers to keep right. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A46
Divided Highway Ends warns that a median will no longer separate opposing traffic and directs drivers to keep right. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A46
A Two Way Traffic sign warns of traffic travelling in opposite directions on the current or upcoming road. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

Misconceptions: Added-lane and lane-ending signs describe different merging needs; a railroad quiet-zone sign does not remove crossing duties.
Mnemonics: Read the shape, identify the message, take the indicated action.
Glossary: A pennant marks a no-passing zone; a crossbuck identifies a rail crossing; channelizing devices guide traffic through a work zone.
Dynamic facts: Live contact details, services and variable fees are withheld from this stable inventory.
